---
name: motion-sdk
description: Motion.page SDK animation library. Use when writing animations with @motion.page/sdk, creating scroll-triggered animations, page transitions, custom cursors, gesture controls, text splitting effects, or any Motion.page SDK code. Activates when code imports from @motion.page/sdk or when the user asks to animate elements.
---

# Motion.page SDK

Package: `@motion.page/sdk` — zero runtime dependencies, zero peer dependencies.

```bash
bun add @motion.page/sdk
# or: npm install @motion.page/sdk
```

---

## Core Pattern

Every animation is a **named timeline**. The name is a registry key — `Motion('same-name')` always returns the same `Timeline` instance.

```ts
import { Motion } from '@motion.page/sdk';

Motion('hero', '#hero', {
  from: { opacity: 0, y: 50 },
  duration: 0.8,
  ease: 'power2.out',
}).play();
```

---

## `from` / `to` Resolution

The SDK automatically resolves the missing endpoint from the element's **current computed CSS**:

| Config | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| `from` only | SDK reads current CSS as `to`. Use for **reveal animations** — start hidden/offset, animate into natural state |
| `to` only | SDK reads current CSS as `from`. Use for **hover/exit effects** — start at natural state, animate to custom values |
| Both | Both endpoints explicit. Only needed when **neither** endpoint matches the element's natural CSS |

**Natural CSS defaults** — omit these from `to` when present:
`opacity: 1` · `x: 0` · `y: 0` · `z: 0` · `scale: 1` · `scaleX: 1` · `scaleY: 1` · `rotate: 0`

```ts
// ✅ from-only — reveal: start hidden, animate to natural state
from: { opacity: 0, y: 50 }

// ✅ to-only — hover: start at natural state, animate to custom values
to: { scale: 1.05, backgroundColor: '#0099ff' }

// ✅ Both needed — parallax: neither endpoint is the element's natural state
from: { x: -50 }
to:   { x: 50 }

// ❌ Redundant — opacity:1 and y:0 are natural defaults, drop the to entirely
from: { opacity: 0, y: 50 }
to:   { opacity: 1, y: 0 }
```

---

## Three Overloads

```ts
// 1. Retrieve existing timeline
Motion(name: string): Timeline

// 2. Single-animation timeline
Motion(name: string, target: TargetInput, config: AnimationConfig): Timeline

// 3. Multi-step timeline
Motion(name: string, animations: AnimationEntry[]): Timeline
```

**`TargetInput`** accepts: CSS selector string, `string[]`, `Element`, `NodeList`, `Element[]`, plain object, or array of plain objects (for non-DOM tweening).

---

## Trigger Methods (chained on `Timeline`)

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `.play()` | Play immediately |
| `.onHover(config?)` | Play on mouseenter, react on mouseleave |
| `.onClick(config?)` | Toggle on click |
| `.onScroll(config?)` | Scrub or snap to scroll position |
| `.onMouseMove(config?)` | Drive progress from mouse position |
| `.onPageLoad(config?)` | Play when DOM is ready (fires immediately if already loaded). `paused: true` builds timeline without playing — start manually with `Motion(name).play()` |
| `.onPageExit(config?)` | Intercept link clicks, play then navigate |
| `.onGesture(config)` | Pointer/touch/wheel/scroll gesture mapping |
| `.onCursor(config)` | Replace native cursor with animated custom cursor |

---

## Static Methods

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `Motion.set(target, vars)` | Immediately apply properties (zero-duration animation) |
| `Motion.get(name)` | Get timeline by name; `undefined` if not found |
| `Motion.has(name)` | Check if named timeline exists |
| `Motion.getNames()` | Array of all registered timeline names |
| `Motion.kill(name)` | Kill one timeline by name, restore initial CSS |
| `Motion.killAll()` | Kill all timelines |
| `Motion.reset(targets)` | Kill animations, revert text splits, clear transform cache |
| `Motion.refreshScrollTriggers()` | Recalculate scroll positions after layout changes |
| `Motion.cleanup()` | Remove ScrollTrigger spacer/marker DOM nodes |
| `Motion.context(fn)` | Create scoped context tracking all timelines in `fn()`. Returns `MotionContext` with `revert()`, `refresh()`, `add()`. For dynamic content reinit. |
| `Motion.responsive(name, variants, breakpoints)` | Register a reactive responsive timeline. Live-swaps per-breakpoint variants as the viewport crosses a boundary (see below). Returns a `ResponsiveManager` (`getActiveTier()`, `destroy()`), or `undefined` if the responsive runtime is not bundled. |
| `Motion.utils` | GSAP-compatible utilities (see below) |

### Motion.utils

```ts
Motion.utils.toArray(target, scope?)     // CSS selector → Element[]
Motion.utils.clamp(min, max, value?)     // Clamp (curried if value omitted)
Motion.utils.random(min, max, snap?)     // Random number
Motion.utils.snap(snapTo, value?)        // Snap to increment or array value
Motion.utils.interpolate(start, end, p) // Linear interpolation (lerp)
Motion.utils.mapRange(inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax, value?)
Motion.utils.normalize(min, max, value?)
Motion.utils.wrap(min, max, value?)
```

---

## Timeline Methods

```ts
// Playback
tl.play(from?: number): this
tl.pause(atTime?: number): this
tl.reverse(from?: number): this
tl.restart(): this
tl.seek(position: number): this

// State (getter/setter — call with no arg to read, with arg to set+return this)
tl.duration(): number
tl.progress(value?: number): number | this
tl.time(value?: number): number | this
tl.timeScale(value?: number): number | this
tl.isActive(): boolean
tl.getName(): string | undefined

// Callbacks at positions
tl.call(callback, params?, position?): this

// Lifecycle callbacks
tl.onStart(cb: () => void): this
tl.onUpdate(cb: (progress: number, time: number) => void): this
tl.onComplete(cb: () => void): this

// Cleanup
tl.kill(clearProps?: boolean): void   // clearProps=true (default) restores CSS
tl.clear(): this                      // Reset and rebuild without destroying
```

## AnimationConfig Quick Shape

```ts
interface AnimationConfig {
  from?:              AnimationVars;          // Start values
  to?:                AnimationVars;          // End values
  duration?:          number;                 // Seconds
  delay?:             number;                 // Seconds before start
  ease?:              string;                 // e.g. 'power2.out', 'elastic.out'
  stagger?:           number | StaggerVars;   // Per-element delay
  repeat?:            number | RepeatConfig;  // -1 = infinite
  split?:             'chars' | 'words' | 'lines' | 'chars,words' | 'words,lines' | 'chars,words,lines';
  mask?:              boolean;                // overflow:hidden clip for reveal effects
  flap?: {
    type:             'flip' | 'fade' | 'slide' | 'blur' | 'scale' | 'board' | 'none';
    charset?:         'alphanumeric' | 'alpha' | 'numeric' | 'symbols' | 'binary' | 'hex' | 'katakana' | 'braille' | string;
    cycles?:          number | [number, number]; // Fixed count or [min, max] random range
    perspective?:     number;               // 3D depth (flip/board only)
    styledBoard?:     boolean;              // Decorative flip-board cells (board only)
    stableWidth?:     boolean | 'cells' | 'container'; // Pin cell widths ('cells'/true) or just outer width ('container')
    preserveWhitespaceCells?: boolean;      // Animate spaces as placeholder cells
  };
  fit?: {
    target: string;      // CSS selector of destination element
    absolute?: boolean;  // Use absolute positioning during animation
    scale?: boolean;     // Include scale changes (default: true, can distort content)
    resize?: boolean;    // Animate width/height instead of scale (no distortion)
  };
  axis?:              'x' | 'y';             // Axis binding for onMouseMove
  onStart?:           () => void;
  onUpdate?:          (progress: number) => void;
  onComplete?:        () => void;
  onRepeat?:          (repeatCount: number) => void;
  onReverseComplete?: () => void;
}
```

**AnimationVars** (common properties):
```ts
x, y, z                        // px by default
rotate, rotateX, rotateY       // deg by default
scale, scaleX, scaleY          // unitless
opacity                        // 0–1
backgroundColor, color         // CSS color string
filter                         // CSS filter string
width, height, top, left       // px or string
fontSize, letterSpacing        // px or string
borderRadius                   // px or string
fill, stroke                   // SVG color
drawSVG                        // string | { start?: number; end?: number }
clipPath, 'clip-path'          // CSS clip-path shape function string (same shape on both ends)
transformOrigin                // string (e.g. 'center', '50% 50%', '0% 100%')
skewX, skewY                   // deg by default
path                           // PathConfig object
'--css-var'                    // Any CSS custom property
```

---

## Key Concepts

### `each: true` — Independent Per-Element Instances

Without `each`, all matched elements share one timeline (group behavior).
With `each`, every element gets its own independent timeline instance.

```ts
// Group — hovering any card plays all
Motion('cards', '.card', { to: { y: -8 }, duration: 0.3 }).onHover({ onLeave: 'reverse' });

// Independent — each card animates on its own
Motion('cards', '.card', { to: { y: -8 }, duration: 0.3 }).onHover({ each: true, onLeave: 'reverse' });
```

Supported in: `.onHover()`, `.onClick()`, `.onScroll()`, `.onMouseMove()`, `.onGesture()`.


### `repeat`

```ts
repeat: -1                               // infinite
repeat: 3                                // 3 additional cycles
repeat: { times: -1, yoyo: true }        // infinite yoyo
repeat: { times: 2, delay: 0.5, yoyo: true }
```

### Timeline Repeat
Loop the entire timeline (all animations replay as a group):

```ts
// Infinite loop
Motion('hero', '.box', { from: { opacity: 0 }, to: { opacity: 1 }, duration: 1 })
  .withRepeat(-1)
  .onPageLoad()

// 3 times with yoyo + delay
Motion('bounce', [entries])
  .withRepeat({ times: 3, yoyo: true, delay: 0.5 })
  .onPageLoad()
```

Accepts same `RepeatConfig | number` as per-animation repeat. Key difference: per-animation `repeat` loops individual animations, `.withRepeat()` loops the whole timeline.

### `split` + `mask` for Text Reveals

```ts
// Characters slide up from behind a clip
Motion('text', 'h1', {
  split: 'lines',
  mask: true,
  from: { y: '100%' },
  stagger: 0.08,
}).onPageLoad();
```

Split elements get data attributes: `data-split-char`, `data-split-word`, `data-split-line` (with index attributes). Inline `<span>` wrappers are preserved.

### `fit` for FLIP Morphing

When `fit` is set, `from`/`to` are ignored — the SDK measures both elements' rects and animates the visual delta.

```ts
Motion('morph', '.source', {
  fit: { target: '.destination', resize: true },  // resize=true avoids text distortion
  duration: 0.5,
  ease: 'power2.inOut',
}).play();
```

### `Motion.responsive()` — Reactive Per-Breakpoint Timelines

Register one named timeline with a **variant factory per breakpoint tier**. The manager picks the tier matching the current viewport and live-swaps as the viewport crosses a boundary — killing the previous tier's timeline (restoring element state, tearing down triggers) and building the new one. No page reload.

```ts
Motion.responsive('hero', {
  desktop: () => Motion('hero', '.hero', { from: { x: -100, opacity: 0 }, duration: 1 }).onPageLoad(),
  phone:   () => Motion('hero', '.hero', { from: { y: 40, opacity: 0 }, duration: 0.6 }).onPageLoad(),
}, { laptops: 992, tablets: 768, phones: 576 });
```

- **Tiers** (cascade order, widest → narrowest): `desktop`, `laptop`, `tablet`, `phone`. The four `matchMedia` ranges are strict and non-overlapping — exactly one matches any width.
- **Each variant is a factory** `() => Timeline | void` that builds **and registers** its timeline (call a trigger like `.onPageLoad()` / `.onScroll()` inside) and returns it so the manager can kill it on the next swap. A factory may return nothing (e.g. all-disabled tier).
- **Sparse maps cascade up**: a missing tier falls back to the nearest wider tier that has a variant. So `{ desktop, phone }` uses `desktop` for laptop/tablet widths.
- **`breakpoints`** are the pixel boundaries `{ laptops, tablets, phones }` (the same values the builder stores). Boundaries: `width > laptops` → desktop, `laptops ≥ width > tablets` → laptop, `tablets ≥ width > phones` → tablet, `width ≤ phones` → phone.
- **Pass the same `name` to `Motion()` inside each variant factory** — only one is active at a time. (The first arg to `Motion.responsive()` itself is not a registry key — each call makes a new manager; `destroy()` the old one before re-registering.)
- Without `matchMedia` (SSR / very old engines) it builds the `desktop` variant once, with no live swapping.
- Tree-shaken: the responsive runtime is only bundled when a project actually uses `Motion.responsive()`.

### Position Syntax

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `0.5` | 0.5s from start (absolute) |
| `"+=0.5"` | 0.5s after previous entry ends |
| `"-=0.3"` | 0.3s before previous entry ends |
| `"<"` | Same start time as previous entry |
| `">"` | Immediately after previous entry ends |
| `"<0.2"` | 0.2s after the START of previous entry |
| `">-0.1"` | 0.1s before the END of previous entry |

### Appending Warning

Calling `Motion(name, target, config)` when `name` already exists **appends** entries rather than replacing. Call `.kill()` first to rebuild:

```ts
Motion('hero').kill();
Motion('hero', '#hero', { from: { opacity: 0 }, duration: 0.8 }).onPageLoad();
```

### `drawSVG` Format

| Input | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `"0% 100%"` | Full stroke visible |
| `"0% 0%"` | Hidden (good for draw-in start) |
| `"20% 80%"` | Middle portion only |
| `"50%"` | Shorthand for `"0% 50%"` |
| `"100px 500px"` | Pixel range |
| `{ start: 20, end: 80 }` | Object — values are **percentages 0–100** (not 0–1) |

### `clip-path` Format

Animate the CSS `clip-path` property between matching shape functions. Use kebab-case `'clip-path'` or camelCase `clipPath`. The renderer also writes `-webkit-clip-path` for older Safari.

| Shape | Example |
|-------|---------|
| `circle` | `'circle(50% at 50% 50%)'` |
| `ellipse` | `'ellipse(60% 30% at 50% 50%)'` |
| `inset` | `'inset(10px 20px round 8px)'` |
| `polygon` | `'polygon(0% 0%, 100% 0%, 100% 100%, 0% 100%)'` |
| `rect` | `'rect(10px 90px 90px 10px)'` |
| `xywh` | `'xywh(10% 10% 80% 80%)'` |

**Rules:**
- **Same shape on both ends** for smooth interpolation. Cross-shape (e.g. `circle → inset`) hard-swaps at progress ≥ 0.5.
- **`polygon` vertex counts must match** between `from` and `to` for smooth morphing.
- Units are preserved (`%`, `px`).
- Use `from`-only or `to`-only — the SDK reads the missing endpoint from the element's current computed `clip-path`.

```ts
// Reveal — circle expands from center
Motion('reveal', '#hero', {
  from: { 'clip-path': 'circle(0% at 50% 50%)' },
  to:   { 'clip-path': 'circle(75% at 50% 50%)' },
  duration: 1,
  ease: 'power2.out',
}).onPageLoad();

// Hover wipe — diagonal polygon driven by hover (camelCase form)
Motion('wipe', '.card', {
  from: { clipPath: 'polygon(0% 0%, 100% 0%, 100% 100%, 0% 100%)' },
  to:   { clipPath: 'polygon(0% 0%, 0% 0%, 100% 100%, 0% 100%)' },
  duration: 0.5,
  ease: 'power2.inOut',
}).onHover({ onLeave: 'reverse' });
```

## Common Patterns

### Fade In on Scroll

```ts
Motion('reveal', '.card', {
  from: { opacity: 0, y: 40 },
  duration: 0.6,
  ease: 'power2.out',
}).onScroll({ scrub: false, toggleActions: 'play none none none' });
```

### Hover Card Lift

```ts
Motion('card-hover', '.card', {
  to: { y: -8, boxShadow: '0 12px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)' },
  duration: 0.3,
  ease: 'power2.out',
}).onHover({ each: true, onLeave: 'reverse' });
```

### Text Reveal with Stagger

```ts
Motion('headline', 'h1', {
  split: 'words',
  mask: true,
  from: { y: '110%' },
  duration: 0.6,
  stagger: { each: 0.06, from: 'start' },
  ease: 'power3.out',
}).onPageLoad();
```

### Paused Page Load (manual trigger)

```ts
// Build timeline on load but don't play — trigger manually with .play()
Motion('hero', '.box', { from: { opacity: 0 }, to: { opacity: 1 }, duration: 1 })
  .onPageLoad({ paused: true })

Motion('hero').play()
```

### Page Exit Transition

```ts
Motion('exit', 'body', {
  to: { opacity: 0 },
  duration: 0.4,
  ease: 'power2.in',
}).onPageExit({ skipHref: ['anchor', 'mailto'] });
```

### Horizontal Scroll with Pin

```ts
const sections = Motion.utils.toArray('.section');
Motion('h-scroll', '.panel', {
  to: { x: `-${(sections.length - 1) * 100}%` },
  duration: 1,
}).onScroll({
  scrub: true,
  pin: true,
  start: 'top top',
  end: `+=${sections.length * 100}%`,
  snap: 1 / (sections.length - 1),
});
```

### Custom Cursor

```ts
Motion('cursor', 'body', { to: { opacity: 1 }, duration: 0 }).onCursor({
  smooth: 0.08,
  hideNative: true,
  default: { width: 12, height: 12, borderRadius: '50%', backgroundColor: '#fff' },
  hover: {
    targets: ['a', 'button', '[data-hover]'],
    width: 40,
    height: 40,
    backgroundColor: 'transparent',
    border: '2px solid white',
    duration: 0.2,
  },
  click: { scale: 0.8, duration: 0.1 },
});
```

---

## Anti-Patterns

| DON'T | DO instead |
|-------|-----------|
| `from: { opacity: 0, y: 50 }, to: { opacity: 1, y: 0 }` | `from: { opacity: 0, y: 50 }` — `opacity:1` and `y:0` are natural defaults, SDK fills them in |
| `import from '@motion/sdk'` | `import from '@motion.page/sdk'` |
| Call `Motion('name', ...)` twice expecting replacement | Call `Motion('name').kill()` first |
| Target multiple independent elements without `each: true` | Add `each: true` to the trigger config |
| Looping with `querySelectorAll().forEach()` to create per-element instances | Simpler: pass selector directly with `each: true` — `Motion('cards', '.card', {...}).onHover({ each: true })` |
| Mix `gsap` + Motion SDK | Use Motion SDK exclusively |
| Use `{ start: 0.2, end: 0.8 }` thinking they're fractions | These are **percentages 0–100** for `drawSVG` objects |
| Use `playNext`/`playPrevious` without `each: true` | Always combine with `each: true` |
| `Hover`/`HoverEnd` gesture events on `window` | Always specify a `target` element for hover events |

---

## Dynamic Content & SPA Pattern

Use `Motion.context()` to scope animations for clean teardown and reinit when DOM content changes (AJAX filters, SPA navigation, infinite scroll, pagination).

```ts
// Create a context — tracks all timelines created inside
const ctx = Motion.context(() => {
  Motion('hero', '.title', { from: { opacity: 0, y: 30 }, duration: 0.8 }).onPageLoad()
  Motion('cards', '.card', { from: { y: 100 }, duration: 1 }).onScroll({ scrub: true })
})

// After dynamic content change (AJAX filter, pagination, etc.):
ctx.refresh()  // kills old animations, re-runs init, re-resolves selectors

// React cleanup on unmount:
// return () => ctx.revert()
```

### React
```ts
useEffect(() => {
  const ctx = Motion.context(() => {
    Motion('fade', '.box', { from: { opacity: 0 }, duration: 0.6 }).onScroll({ scrub: true })
  })
  return () => ctx.revert()
}, [])
```

### Astro (View Transitions)
```ts
let ctx: MotionContext | undefined
document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', () => {
  ctx?.revert()
  ctx = Motion.context(() => { /* animations */ })
})
```

### WordPress (automatic)
The WordPress plugin wraps animation code in `Motion.context()` automatically. Call `MOTIONPAGE_FRONT.reinit()` after AJAX content changes.

### Legacy cleanup (without context)
```ts
Motion.killAll();
Motion.cleanup();
```
